slots.evidence: Recognize a specific bit mismatch between instructor-labelled sent and received sequences.
Recognize a rule-derived parity bit as extra checking information shared by sender and receiver.
Apply a stated even/odd rule to a complete transmitted sequence including the appended bit.
Apply the agreed parity rule to a complete received frame and interpret the pass/fail observation.

blueprint.c1_structural_anchor: At least one correct, meaningful and usable parity construction or receiver check aspect constitutes minimum U evidence; integrated account is not required for 1 point.
blueprint.form_equivalence: Parallel four-item C1 roles, equal-length six-bit subjective frames; empirical equivalence not established.
blueprint.form_assignment: Allocate sets A/B/C independently of pedagogy; balance assignment across treatments and record chosen set and frozen delivered order.

subjective.grade_using: private.subjective_resolved.contract + private.subjective_resolved.case (verified receiver fact fields only) + exact public.subjective.prompt + raw learner response
subjective.meaning_of_null: technical/scientific grading ambiguity; review hold, NOT zero
subjective.judge_blinding: Do not pass pedagogy, Tutor history, MCQs, MCQ score, prior attempts, or learner identity to Assessment Judge.

existing_v05_scoring_gate_reference.use: Existing backend scoring rule; not a declaration of validated SOLO state.

mcqs.stem: An instructor compares the five bits actually sent (11001) with the five bits received (10001), reading positions from left to right starting at 1. Which statement accurately describes the difference?

options.text: Position 3 changed from 0 to 1.
No bit changed because both sequences contain five bits.
Position 2 changed from 1 to 0.
Position 2 changed from 0 to 1.

mcqs.stem: Why does a sender append a parity bit to the original data?

options.text: It adds checking information calculated from the data using a rule that sender and receiver share.
It stores an extra full copy of each original data bit.
It always tells the receiver exactly which bit changed.
It is chosen randomly because its value does not affect the check.

mcqs.stem: A sender has the payload 10100 and appends one bit on the right using odd parity. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Append 0: 101000 contains two 1s and therefore meets odd parity.
Append 1: 101001 contains four 1s and therefore meets odd parity.
Append 0 because an appended parity bit is excluded from the parity check.
Append 1: 101001 contains three 1s and therefore meets odd parity.

subjective.prompt: The receiver gets the six-bit sequence 010101, including the rightmost parity bit. Using even parity, does the check pass or fail? Explain your check and what the result tells the receiver.

option_feedback.B: Equal sequence length does not imply equal bit values.
option_feedback.C: Position 2 is 1 in sent and 0 in received.
option_feedback.D: Reverses the direction of the actual position-2 flip.

mcqs.correct_answer: It adds checking information calculated from the data using a rule that sender and receiver share.

oracle.principle: Parity bit is added redundancy fixed by original data and an agreed parity convention.

option_feedback.B: One appended bit is not a full copy of the payload.
option_feedback.C: Single parity failure does not identify a changed position.
option_feedback.D: An arbitrary bit would not reliably satisfy the agreed parity rule.

mcqs.correct_answer: Append 1: 101001 contains three 1s and therefore meets odd parity.

option_feedback.A: Two ones is even, not odd.
option_feedback.C: The appended check bit is included in the complete parity check.
option_feedback.D: Correct: adding 1 makes the full sequence have three ones.

contract.target_structural_evidence: Basic, usable receiver parity checking is sufficient for minimum U evidence; sender reconstruction is not required.

score_anchor.0: No usable correct parity-checking evidence, or a central contradiction that undermines the attempted check.
score_anchor.1: At least one meaningful correct receiver-check aspect with a recognizable rule-based reason (for example, correctly counting the ones or applying the specified parity convention), but an incomplete or incorrectly concluded check.
score_anchor.2: Correctly evaluates the complete six-bit received sequence including the check bit, gives the correct pass/fail result with a clear parity-based reason, and interprets what the receiver can conclude without an unsupported guarantee.

evidence_elements.complete_group: Count all six received bits in 010101, including the rightmost checking bit.
evidence_elements.ones_count: The complete received sequence has 3 ones.
evidence_elements.criterion: An even number of ones is required.
evidence_elements.interpretation: FAIL detects a violation of the agreed parity rule; it does not reveal which bit changed or repair it.

legitimate_alternative_explanations: Accept correct odd/even reasoning without the numeric count when the logic is explicit.
Accept plain-language terms such as matches, satisfies, broken, violates, consistent, detected error.
Do not require a sender payload, sender-side derivation, original transmission, or a particular example sentence.
material_invalidators: Excluding the received parity bit from the complete check.
Reversing the agreed even/odd convention as a matter of principle.
Claiming a passing check guarantees no error or that a failed check identifies/corrects the changed bit.
full_credit_blockers: A wrong final result despite otherwise correct numerical work.
A correct PASS/FAIL guess with no recognizable parity-rule explanation.
A material false conclusion about detection, guarantee, localization, or correction.
contract.contradiction_handling: Score demonstrated usable reasoning, not isolated labels. An essential contradiction that negates the central mechanism scores 0; a minor unrelated overclaim blocks 2. Borderline internally inconsistent answers may require review.

mcqs.stem: An instructor compares the five bits sent (00110) with the five bits received (00111), numbering positions from the left starting at 1. What happened?

options.text: Position 4 changed from 1 to 0.
Position 5 changed from 0 to 1.
No transmission bit changed.
Position 5 changed from 1 to 0.

mcqs.stem: What must be true for a parity bit to serve as meaningful checking information at the receiver?

options.text: The sender may choose 0 or 1 arbitrarily after sending the data.
The receiver must possess a pristine copy of the original data.
The appended parity bit must always be 1.
The sender determines the extra bit from the data using a parity convention also known to the receiver.

mcqs.stem: A sender has the payload 11010 and appends one bit on the right using even parity. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Append 1: 110101 contains four 1s and meets even parity.
Append 0: 110100 contains four 1s and meets even parity.
Append 1, but check only the original five data bits to decide whether the full sequence is even.
Append 0 because an even-parity full sequence must have an odd number of 1s.

subjective.prompt: The receiver gets the six-bit sequence 101010, including the rightmost parity bit. Using odd parity, does the check pass or fail? Explain your check and what the result tells the receiver.

option_feedback.B: Position 5 was 0 in sent bits and is 1 in received bits.

mcqs.correct_answer: The sender determines the extra bit from the data using a parity convention also known to the receiver.

oracle.principle: Checking information is derived under a shared rule; received message itself is checked.

option_feedback.A: An arbitrary bit may violate the intended parity convention.
option_feedback.B: Receiver does not ordinarily require an uncorrupted original copy.
option_feedback.C: The correct check bit depends on payload and convention.
option_feedback.D: Correct role of deterministic agreed checking information.

mcqs.correct_answer: Append 1: 110101 contains four 1s and meets even parity.

option_feedback.A: Correct: four ones in the complete frame.
option_feedback.B: 110100 has three ones, not four; it fails even parity.
option_feedback.C: The appended bit must be included in the full-frame parity check.
option_feedback.D: Even parity requires an even number of ones.

mcqs.stem: An instructor shows a five-bit sequence sent as 10001 and received as 10011. Positions are numbered left to right from 1. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: Position 3 changed from 0 to 1.
Position 5 changed from 1 to 0.
Both sequences are identical.
Position 4 changed from 0 to 1.

mcqs.stem: Which description of a parity bit is correct?

options.text: It replaces one original data bit to shorten the message.
It is a random extra bit that the receiver ignores.
It is extra transmitted checking information whose value depends on the data and a parity rule shared by both ends.
It guarantees that the receiver can restore the original message after any error.

mcqs.stem: A sender has the payload 00111 and appends one bit on the right using odd parity. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Append 1: 001111 has four 1s and meets odd parity.
Append 0: 001110 has three 1s and meets odd parity.
Append 0: 001110 has two 1s and meets odd parity.
Append 1 because an odd-parity check bit is always 1.

subjective.prompt: The receiver gets the six-bit sequence 111000, including the rightmost parity bit. Using even parity, does the check pass or fail? Explain your check and what the result tells the receiver.

mcqs.correct_answer: It is extra transmitted checking information whose value depends on the data and a parity rule shared by both ends.

oracle.principle: Parity bit is rule-derived redundancy and supports checking, not arbitrary correction.

option_feedback.A: Parity adds a bit instead of replacing original payload data.
option_feedback.B: The check bit is rule-derived and included in checking.
option_feedback.D: Single parity does not guarantee error correction.

mcqs.correct_answer: Append 0: 001110 has three 1s and meets odd parity.

option_feedback.A: Four ones is even, not odd.
option_feedback.B: Correct: three ones in the complete frame.
option_feedback.C: 001110 actually has three ones; the stated count is incorrect.
option_feedback.D: Check-bit value depends on the existing payload.
